probes.query: Under every documented member the generated pages tell the reader where in the code base it is defined, and for most projects that line is a clickable address on the code host instead of plain text. When the user supplied no address pattern of their own, trace how that address is worked out, from the very start of a run to the final markup, and say which source files end up with a plain, non-clickable line.
expectedFacts: Application.initializeRepositories (application.ts, awaited from convert before conversion starts) builds a RepositoryManager and asks it to initialize repositories for every directory that holds a source file of the programs.

CRITICAL: GitRepository.tryCreateRepository, when no link pattern was configured, reads the remote's URL with the git command line and derives the pattern with guessSourceUrlTemplate (recognises GitHub, GitHub-enterprise, Bitbucket and GitLab hosts).
GitRepository.getURL fills the pattern placeholders (revision, short revision, path relative to the repository root, line); the revision is git's HEAD commit (or the branch name when requested).

CRITICAL: GitRepository.getURL returns undefined for any file that is not in the repository's tracked-file list (git ls-files), so untracked or ignored files, and files outside every repository, get no address.
SourcePlugin.onBeginResolve sets each source reference's url from repositories.getURL(fullFileName, line) and rewrites its shown file name relative to a base path.
member.sources.tsx sourceLink prints plain file:line text when the reference has no url and an anchor otherwise.

navigation.tsx settings() renders a box for protected, private and external members only when the matching exclusion setting is off, always renders the inherited one, and renders one per '@' key (box name = key without '@', camel case turned into kebab case).
ImplementsPlugin's createLink sets the Inherited reflection flag on a member that comes from a base class (and not on one that overrides it) while conversion runs.

probes.query: The sidebar tree of a generated site is not part of each page's markup. Trace how that tree travels from the documentation model into a visitor's browser and gets drawn there, including how it is kept small and what the page does while waiting for it.
expectedFacts: NavigationPlugin registers its job only when the active theme is the default theme; the job is queued among the pre-render async jobs and runs before any page file is written.

CRITICAL: The job calls DefaultTheme.getNavigation, which caches buildNavigation's result for the render; buildNavigation builds nested NavigationElements from modules, groups, categories and folder-like module names, honouring the navigation flag setting and the leaf-name list.
CRITICAL: compressJson JSON-stringifies the tree, deflates it with zlib and base64-encodes it; NavigationPlugin writes it as window.navigationData in assets/navigation.js.

layouts/default.tsx loads that script asynchronously under an id that the browser code listens on, and navigation.tsx renders an empty list container that shows a loading entry until the tree is built.

Navigation.ts initNav waits for the script's load event (or runs at once), decodes the data with decompressJson (atob, DecompressionStream deflate, JSON.parse) and builds nested details/summary elements and links relative to the page's base address.

linkResolver.resolveLinkTag asks the external resolvers only after it found no documented target, both for a TypeScript-resolved symbol id with no reflections and for a parsed declaration reference that resolveDeclarationReference cannot resolve; a string (or object with target/caption) result becomes the link part's target.

CRITICAL: validation/links.ts treats a link part as broken only when it has no target or its target is still a ReflectionSymbolId, so a string target coming from the mapping is not reported.

CRITICAL: Both schemes are loaded together once per render by DefaultTheme.preRender (loadHighlighter with the light and dark themes), and ShikiHighlighter.highlight tokenises every block with both themes at once, emitting classes hl-N.

ShikiHighlighter.getStyles produces highlight.css that defines per-class CSS variables for light and dark and selects between them with prefers-color-scheme media queries and :root[data-theme] rules; AssetsPlugin writes that file.
